newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest direct hogs seen steady-off $1 -dealers.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest direct hogs seen steady-off $1 -dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices were seen steady to $1.00 per cwt lower on Thursday, pressured by outlooks for ongoing heavy marketings, livestock dealers said.

Widespread rain in Iowa and Illinois on Wednesday and forecasts for rain in Indiana and Ohio overnight were expected to make fields too muddy for planting, which would allow farmers time to catch up on hog marketings, they said.
Interior Iowa/southern Minnesota top prices for hogs at plants were seen at $58.00 to $58.50 and Illinois top prices were expected at $57.00 to $57.50, dealers in those areas said.
Indiana/Ohio tops at plants could range $57.50-$58.00.

But talk circulated that price declines could be limited if many of the hogs held back by planting were already sold on Tuesday and Wednesday when more hogs came to market than were expected, some sources noted.

Interior Iowa/southern Minnesota hog movement Tuesday totaled 104,000 head, USDA said, above the agency's estimate of 95,000. Wednesday's estimate was 105,000 head, above 90,000 last week and 99,000 last year.
If receipts come in light Thursday despite the rain, it could indicate a currentness in hog marketings. That in turn could boost cash hog prices, some sources said.
